scoring_justification: The headline metric is a stress-strain curve; T1 recompute from raw agent artifacts is infeasible because the full laminate solver cannot be re-run in the verifier. Therefore we compare the agent's reported curve to a hidden gold curve digitized from the paper, with tolerance to account for implementation differences.

hidden_assets.purpose: gold stress-strain reference curve and uniform-deformation stress threshold
hidden_assets.source_provenance: digitized from Fig. 2 of the paper; stress values consistent with Hutchinson-Pierce hardening for Al-Cu alloy with q=1.4, τ0=100 MPa, τs=180 MPa, h0=541.5 MPa
hidden_assets.generation_method: manual reconstruction from the paper's graphical data and physical reasoning about the softening magnitude
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: the curve closely approximates the published experimental computational result; the uniform stress threshold is derived from the double-slip hardening curve displayed in the same figure

outputs.description: Macroscopic resolved shear stress vs. shear strain curve for an fcc crystal under simple shear on (001)[110], computed with the local sequential lamination theory. The file must contain at least 20 data points covering the strain range up to at least 0.1.

output_contract.notes: The agent's curve will be compared to a hidden reference curve. The evaluation also checks that the curve exhibits softening relative to the uniform double-slip response.
